topic: How FX-options desks actually use Excel: the pricing (read) path and the contribution (write) path, cell-level UX, and why Excel persists — mapped to Celnet's single unversioned contract and OSS-only constraints
summary: Excel remains the universal "last mile" of every FX-options desk: traders, structurers and risk managers live in a grid even when a dedicated GUI exists, because Excel is where ad-hoc analytics, blotters and bespoke risk views get assembled in seconds. Desks use it two ways. (1) PRICING / read-path: pull live and historical vanilla/exotic prices, the full Greek set, and the vol surface (ATM/RR/BF per tenor, smile, 3D) into cells, plus scenario/risk grids. The critical distinction is streaming (RTD / Office.js streaming custom functions, two-way live prices that re-tick autonomously) vs static snapshots (a one-shot promise-resolving function or a frozen paste). The desk builds three recurring sheet archetypes — a pricer (single-deal calculator), a blotter (one option per row, columns of price+Greeks), and a risk sheet (aggregated Greeks/ladders/scenario shocks). (2) CONTRIBUTION / write-path: the trader marks a surface from Excel (ATM/RR/BF overrides per tenor), contributes a two-way quote, or applies a what-if override — and this MUST be wrapped by entitlement, validation (arb-free checks), audit and four-eyes/maker-checker, because a write mutates shared firm state. Excel persists despite well-known failure modes (stale RTD, #N/A storms, blocking calls freezing the grid, convention ambiguity) because of zero-friction composability. For Celnet specifically: the read path maps to RFS streaming subscriptions surfaced as streaming custom functions, the write path maps to the existing surface mark / click-to-trade / what-if-override services on the ONE current contract, and the add-in must be OSS-only (Office.js / web-stack add-in; NO PyXLL or commercial XLL SDK) and never fork the wire contract.
key_findings: READ-PATH, the three canonical sheets a desk builds. PRICER: a single-deal calculator block where the trader types pair/notional/expiry/strike-or-delta/style into input cells and reads price + full Greeks from output cells, re-pricing live as spot/vol tick. BLOTTER: one FX option per row, with formula columns producing price and the Greek set per row (=CELNET.PRICE(...), =CELNET.DELTA(...)); the desk's working position. RISK SHEET: aggregation of the blotter into bucketed Greeks (vega by tenor/delta pillar, gamma/theta ladders) plus scenario/what-if shock grids (spot bumps x vol bumps). These three are universal across FX-options desks.

READ-PATH, the full Greek set a desk expects in cells is broader than retail Delta/Gamma/Vega/Theta/Rho: FX desks specifically want the vol-of-vol family — Vanna (dDelta/dVol), Volga/Vomma (dVega/dVol), and often Charm, Speed, Zomma, plus dual-delta. Celnet already computes a 13-Greek set, so the read API must expose all of them per-cell, not a reduced subset.

READ-PATH, the vol surface is consumed in three shapes simultaneously: (a) market quote convention per tenor — ATM, 25d/10d Risk-Reversal, 25d/10d Butterfly (the desk's native vocabulary, NOT raw vols); (b) the smile (vol vs strike-or-delta for one tenor) for charting; (c) the full 3D surface (tenor x delta -> vol) spilled into a grid for term-structure/skew analysis. The desk reads in ATM/RR/BF because that is how the broker market quotes; raw per-strike vols are a derived view.

READ-PATH, STREAMING vs SNAPSHOT is the single most important semantic. Streaming = the cell re-ticks autonomously as the market moves (live two-way prices, surface re-marks); implemented via Excel RTD (legacy COM ProgID server) or modern Office.js streaming custom functions (invocation.setResult called repeatedly; WebSocket-backed). Snapshot = a one-shot value resolved once (promise-returning async function, or a manual freeze/paste-values) used for marking a moment, EOD marks, or trade-capture so the number cannot move under the trader. A desk needs BOTH and needs an explicit, obvious way to freeze a streaming cell into a snapshot.

READ-PATH, recalculation pitfalls are real and cell-level. (i) RTD/streaming cells do NOT respond to F2/Enter or Ctrl+Alt+F9 — normal recalc cannot force them; they tick on their own schedule. (ii) Volatile functions (NOW/RAND/OFFSET-style) recompute on every calc and, chained with live data, can thrash the calc tree and starve the grid. (iii) Dynamic-array SPILL: a surface returned as a single spilled array is elegant but throws #SPILL! if any cell in the spill target is occupied, and a blocked/erroring root spill propagates errors to every dependent downstream cell instantly. (iv) Manual calc mode can leave spill ranges and dependents stale. The add-in should prefer per-cell streaming scalars OR carefully-sized spill blocks, and document calc-mode behavior.

WRITE-PATH (CONTRIBUTION) is categorically different from pricing: it MUTATES shared firm state, so it is not just a formula. The three concrete contribution actions are: (1) MARK A SURFACE — the trader overrides ATM/RR/BF for one or more tenors from input cells and commits, producing a new calibrated, arb-free marked surface; (2) CONTRIBUTE A TWO-WAY QUOTE — push a bid/offer (vol or premium) for a specific deal/RFQ back to the system/counterparty; (3) WHAT-IF OVERRIDE — a private, non-committed scenario surface/spot used only for the trader's own pricing without touching the firm mark. Maps directly to Celnet's existing MarkSurface (versioned surface registry), click-to-trade tradable-token execute, and a scenario/override path.

WRITE-PATH controls are mandatory and must wrap every contribution: ENTITLEMENT (who may mark which pair/tenor — control-plane identity, e.g. Celnet's keyed-MAC session token, never a pricing input so determinism is preserved); VALIDATION (server-side arb-free / sanity checks on the proposed ATM/RR/BF before acceptance — reject, don't silently accept, mirroring the existing DegenerateQuote guard); AUDIT (immutable who/what/when/old->new record of every mark and quote, for compliance reconstruction); FOUR-EYES / MAKER-CHECKER (a second authorized user approves a mark before it becomes the firm's official surface; trader marks, supervisor confirms). The Excel cell-level UX is: edit override cells, hit a 'Submit Mark' button (ribbon/task-pane), see a pending state, then a confirmed/rejected state with the surface_version echoed back.

WRITE-PATH must ride the ONE current Celnet contract, never a fork. The mark commit should return the new surface_version so the trader's read-path cells immediately re-pin to their own just-committed surface (closing the read/write loop), and Execute must be idempotent against duplicate clicks (the tradable-token already provides this). What-if overrides resolve against a private/pinned surface_version so they never leak into the firm mark — exactly the unknown-version => failed_precondition semantics already in the server.

WHY EXCEL PERSISTS: zero-friction composability. A trader can wire a bespoke risk view, a custom scenario grid, or a one-off structured-deal pricer in minutes using cells + the desk's pricing functions, with no software release cycle. It is the lingua franca across trading, structuring, sales, risk and middle-office, and it composes the firm's pricing engine with the trader's own logic (hedge ratios, P&L attribution, bespoke baskets). No bespoke GUI ever fully displaces it; the winning strategy is a first-class add-in, not a walled-garden replacement.

FAILURE MODES the add-in must engineer against: (1) STALE RTD — cells silently stop ticking (server drop, lost subscription) while still showing an old value; the trader cannot tell live from frozen. Mitigation: a visible heartbeat/last-update timestamp and an explicit stale indicator per subscription. (2) #N/A STORMS — a transient failure returns notAvailable to many cells at once and cascades through dependents; mitigation: graceful last-good-value with a stale flag rather than blanket #N/A, bounded retry. (3) BLOCKING CALLS FREEZE THE GRID — synchronous/async-but-serialized calls, or high update volume, lock the Excel UI; Excel only ingests updates when in the 'ready' state (an open modal dialog or a cell mid-edit blocks updates), and legacy COM RTD has throttle/message-rate limits. Mitigation: never block the UI thread, push over a bounded queue, coalesce ticks, cap update frequency. (4) CONVENTION AMBIGUITY — the deadliest: a number in a cell with no attached convention (which delta convention, premium-adjusted vs not, spot vs forward delta, ATM definition DNS vs 50d, business-day/cut, domestic vs foreign premium) is dangerous; the same '25d RR' means different things under different conventions. Mitigation: every contributed/consumed value must carry or pin its convention explicitly (Celnet's celnet-conventions/celnet-calendar already model this), and the add-in must surface the convention in the cell/task-pane, never leave it implicit.

TECHNICAL CHOICE for Celnet (OSS-only mandate honored): use the modern Office.js web add-in with STREAMING CUSTOM FUNCTIONS (the @streaming tag / CustomFunctions.StreamingInvocation, calling invocation.setResult repeatedly, backed by a WebSocket to Celnet's RFS stream) for the read path, and a TASK PANE / RIBBON action calling the gRPC/WS contract for the write path. This is permissively-licensed Microsoft tooling (Office.js) plus OSS web stack — explicitly NOT PyXLL or any commercial XLL/add-in SDK. onCanceled must clean up sockets/timers (cancellation ordering vs new invocation is NOT guaranteed); errors map to CustomFunctions.Error(ErrorCode.notAvailable) i.e. #N/A; and note the known Office.js pitfall that a streaming custom function and a same-named legacy COM RTD function must not collide in one cell (crash). Streaming-function cancellation fires on cell edit, arg change, or manual recalc.
recommendations: Ship a Celnet Office.js web add-in (OSS web stack only, no PyXLL/commercial XLL). Read path = streaming custom functions over a WebSocket to the existing RFS stream; write path = task-pane/ribbon actions calling the existing gRPC/WS contract. Both ride the ONE current unversioned contract — the add-in is a thin edge consumer, never a contract fork.

Expose the read path as the three canonical sheets out of the box: a Pricer template (single-deal in/out block), a Blotter template (one option per row, price + full 13-Greek columns), and a Risk template (bucketed vega/gamma/theta + spot x vol scenario grid). Provide ready-made cell functions like CELNET.PRICE / CELNET.GREEK / CELNET.SURFACE(pair,tenor,'RR25') so traders compose their own views in minutes.

Make STREAMING vs SNAPSHOT explicit and first-class: streaming functions for live prices/surface, plus a one-shot snapshot function and a 'freeze to values' ribbon action for marking a moment / trade capture / EOD. Never let a trader be unsure whether a cell is live or frozen — show a per-subscription heartbeat/last-update timestamp and a visible stale indicator.

Implement contribution (write path) for all three actions on the existing services: MarkSurface (ATM/RR/BF override -> new surface_version), click-to-trade two-way quote/execute (idempotent tradable token), and a private what-if override that pins a non-firm surface_version. After a successful mark, return the new surface_version so the trader's read cells re-pin to their own commit, closing the loop.

Wrap every write with the mandatory controls: entitlement via the existing keyed-MAC session token (control-plane identity, NOT a pricing input — preserves bit-determinism); server-side arb-free validation reusing the DegenerateQuote/arb-free guards (reject bad marks, never silently accept); an immutable audit record (who/what/when/old->new/surface_version); and a four-eyes/maker-checker step where a mark is pending until a second entitled user confirms. Surface pending/confirmed/rejected states in the task pane.

Engineer against the four failure modes explicitly: never block the Excel UI thread (push over a bounded queue, coalesce/throttle ticks, respect Excel's 'ready'-state ingestion); degrade to last-good-value + stale flag instead of #N/A storms; clean up sockets/timers in onCanceled (do not assume it fires before the next invocation); and attach an explicit convention to every value (delta convention, premium-adjusted, spot/forward, ATM definition, cut/calendar) surfaced in-cell/task-pane using celnet-conventions + celnet-calendar — convention ambiguity is the highest-severity correctness risk.

Avoid the known Office.js/RTD collision: do not register a streaming custom function and a same-named legacy COM RTD function that can land in the same cell (documented crash). Standardize on Office.js streaming custom functions and do not ship a parallel COM RTD path with name overlap.

Validate the add-in the same way the rest of Celnet is validated: exercise real-like trader/structurer/risk-manager Excel workflows (price a deal, build a blotter, run a scenario grid, mark a surface with four-eyes, contribute a quote) as tests against the live contract, and keep docs (a new docs/EXCEL-ADDIN.md and INTERFACES.md note) in sync — the contribution control model and convention pinning are load-bearing and must be documented, not implicit.
risks: Convention ambiguity is the top correctness risk: an unlabeled '25d RR' or premium in a cell can be misinterpreted across delta conventions (spot vs forward, premium-adjusted vs not), ATM definitions (DNS vs 50d), or cut/calendar — leading to mismarked surfaces and real P&L/risk errors. Every value must carry/pin its convention; leaving it implicit is unacceptable on an institutional desk.

Write-path without rigorous controls is a compliance and operational hazard: an un-entitled, un-audited, single-eyes mark or quote contributed from a spreadsheet can corrupt the firm's official surface or leak a bad price to a counterparty. Four-eyes, entitlement, validation and immutable audit are non-negotiable, not nice-to-haves.

Stale-but-displayed data: RTD/streaming cells can silently stop ticking yet keep showing an old value, so a trader may price/hedge off a dead number believing it is live. Without a visible heartbeat/stale indicator this is a latent risk that surfaces exactly during market stress (when servers drop).

Excel UI-thread blocking and 'ready'-state ingestion: high update volume, synchronous calls, or an open modal/edit can freeze the grid or silently drop updates; legacy COM RTD additionally imposes message-rate throttles. A naive add-in that does not coalesce/throttle and offload work will freeze under a busy market — the opposite of Celnet's latency goals.

Dynamic-array #SPILL fragility: returning the surface as one spilled block is elegant but breaks if the spill target is occupied and propagates errors to all dependents; combined with manual-calc mode this yields stale/erroring risk grids that look authoritative. Spill usage must be deliberate and defensively sized.

Determinism leakage: pricing inputs flowing from Excel must remain pure inputs to the deterministic libm core; the session/entitlement identity (keyed-MAC token) must stay strictly control-plane. Mixing control-plane identity into pricing inputs would break Celnet's bit-identical price guarantee.

Contract-fork temptation: building the add-in against a convenience shim or a versioned/forked schema would violate the single-current-contract rule and create a mixed-version window. The add-in must consume the exact current gRPC/WS contract and surface_version semantics, with no back-compat shim.

Tooling-license trap: it is easy to reach for PyXLL or a commercial XLL/add-in SDK for speed; this violates the OSS-only mandate. Must stay on Office.js + permissive web stack (and OSS XLL crates are acceptable, commercial add-in SDKs are not).

topic: Competitor Excel integrations for FX and derivatives
key_findings: Bloomberg Add-in (BDP BDH BDS BQL BLP-RTD over BLPAPI) is Windows-only, terminal-tethered, 2s RTD throttle, silently stale
Refinitiv forced an Eikon-to-Workspace COM migration; Fenics is data-distribution only
Numerix XL is commercial Windows COM; SuperDerivatives Murex 360T ICE export or display only
Read-only data pipes versus pricing engines; none bridges both; Office.js runs Windows Mac web
recommendations: Office.js add-in over the current gRPC and WebSocket contract; cross-platform; no commercial SDK
Live in-cell pricing: 13 Greeks, exotics, LSV, arb-free surface, deterministic libm, explicit FX conventions
Kill staleness with sequence numbers, surface_version and explicit STALE state at engine cadence
Two-way write-back with click-to-trade tokens; unversioned contract; vendor-neutral namespace
risks: Office.js sandboxed; Mac and web lag desktop APIs; streaming needs WebSocket push
Vendor-neutral namespace adds friction versus BDP RDP; needs credible exotic coverage
Write-back needs server-side permissioning; never re-distribute broker-licensed data

topic: Excel integration for Celnet (Office.js streaming custom functions vs Rust XLL vs COM RTD vs gRPC-web/Connect)
summary: Office.js streaming custom functions over the WS mirror are the primary cross-platform path; an optional OSS Rust XLL serves low-latency Windows desks; both ride the single celnet-proto contract. See key_findings for full analysis, recommendations, and risks (folded due to a tool payload limit).
key_findings: Office.js streaming custom functions are the cross-platform real-time path: streaming JSDoc tag or CustomFunctions.StreamingInvocation param, push via invocation.setResult, clean up in invocation.onCanceled. MS docs endorse a browser WebSocket inside the function for financial tickers, exactly Celnet RFS (custom-functions-web-reqs, 2026-03).
Office.js add-ins are cross-platform (Win/Mac/web) and zero-install via manifest (sideload, M365 admin, AppSource). Only path covering Mac and web.

Excel keys each distinct-arg streaming function as a separate stream, reusing identical-arg streams, mapping onto per-SubscriptionId RFS. onCanceled vs new-invocation ordering is not guaranteed, so subscribe/unsubscribe must be idempotent (matches celnet-client idempotency-key plus Resync).

Custom-functions batching collapses N cell calls into one request via an invocationEntry queue, coalescing many CELNET.PRICE cells into one edge request. Minimize volatile functions; they slow recalc.

Browsers/Office.js cannot client-side or bidi stream over HTTP; gRPC-web and Connect give browsers only unary plus server-streaming. Celnet RFS is bidirectional, so a raw WebSocket (WS mirror) is correct, not gRPC-web/Connect.

Connect (connect-es/connect-web) is the best protobuf-over-fetch TS option: HTTP/1.1/2/3, POST-only, debuggable, better TS/ESM/bundles than Google grpc-web, also speaks gRPC-web. Reuses celnet-proto for unary RPCs. Split: Connect-web unary, WS mirror bidi RFS.

Native Rust XLL is OSS-clean: xladd/xladd-derive/xladd-util (MIT) wrap Excel4/Excel12 LPXLOPER12 C API, auto-derive registration, cdylib, Excel 2007+. Fastest (in-proc) but Windows-only, per-desk install, unsafe; isolate as an edge crate, never the core.

xladd has no RTD/IRTDServer (wish-list), so it gives pull UDFs but must add RTD push. OSS mcgoo/artydee is a hand-written IRtdServer/IRTDUpdateEvent skeleton on the com crate (embed-resources TLB from IDL), a 4-commit not-polished prototype, unclear license. Standalone Rust COM RTD (option c) is heaviest, Windows-only; not primary.

Auth: getAccessToken (legacy SSO) or preferred MSAL Nested App Authentication (NAA); token goes to the edge, OAuth2 OBO mints a downstream identity, OBO tokens server-side. Control-plane only, not a pricing input, so determinism (libm) is untouched, like the keyed-MAC click-to-trade token.

All options reuse the single contract, no fork: Office.js/Connect/XLL all (de)serialize the exact celnet-proto messages. WS mirror must be generated from the same Rust types as gRPC (API-CLIENTS.md s2), so Excel gets identical snapshot/delta/resync and identical prices (rule 9, determinism).
recommendations: PRIMARY celnet-excel Office.js add-in (streaming functions over a browser WebSocket to the WS mirror for CELNET.RFS; unary CELNET.PRICE/QUOTE/SMILE/SCENARIO over Connect-web). Build the WS mirror first by serde-generating the JSON tagged enum from celnet-types. SECONDARY/optional celnet-xll Windows edge crate (xladd/xladd-derive MIT), RTD push only if needed via a hardened artydee-style IRtdServer, all unsafe confined there. Auth via MSAL NAA plus OBO at the edge (control-plane only). Use Office.js batching, minimize volatile functions. Add an ADR and update API-CLIENTS.md/DELIVERY-MODEL.md plus ledger rows.
risks: Commercial add-in SDK ban (rule 7): Office.js plus OSS xladd (MIT) only, connect-es (Apache-2.0) checked via a JS license gate. Native XLL is unsafe, Windows-only, with COM-registration friction. RTD cross-platform fragility (office-js 5175) and streaming bugs (office-js 4083): use one add-in type per deployment, idempotent subscribe/unsubscribe, resync-from-last_seq. WS mirror is unbuilt (prioritize). artydee is a 4-commit prototype, unclear license (reference only). JSON-over-WS floats must round-trip bit-identically via a to_bits-stable f64 encoding tested vs gRPC.
